title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'). 𝔖 is a profinite group of GL(2)-type. It contains an index-2 'orientation-preserving' subgroup 𝔖^+ and a character ε_𝔖: 𝔖 → {±1} with kernel 𝔖^+. The elements involved are: σ ∈ 𝔖^+ with σ² = −1; ρ ∈ 𝔖^+; and τ ∈ 𝔖 with ε_𝔖(τ) = −1, τσ = −στ and τ(ρ) = σ^{-1}(ρ^{-1}), where α(x) denotes conjugation by α. The group μ = {±1} is central. 𝔖^𝔤 ⊂ 𝔖^+ is a normal subgroup, and 𝔖^𝔤_τ = 𝔖^𝔤 ∪ 𝔖^𝔤τ. Grothendieck considers automorphisms u of 𝔖^+ satisfying two conditions. (a) u(ρ) = α(ρ) for some α ∈ 𝔖^𝔤_τ, with ε_𝔖(α) = ε_3. (b) u(σ) ≡ ε_2 σ mod 𝔖^𝔤. He proves that these automorphisms form a group 𝒢_{(a)(b)}; the next page calls it Z_{ρ,σ}. He then compares it with the Teichmüller-tower groups 𝓜[0] and 𝓜^![0] for various choices of 𝔖^𝔤 (𝔖^+, Π = Π_0×μ, Π_0).

The previous page treats ε_3 = +1 and gives α'' = u'(α)α', see (7). For ε_3 = −1 it writes α = α_0τ and obtains (u'u)(ρ) = α''(ρ) with α'' = ε·u'(α_0)u'(σ)α'στ. Here ε ∈ μ is still free, because it is central and does not change the conjugation action.

This page chooses ε so that α'' ∈ 𝔖^𝔤_τ.
- Reduce modulo 𝔖^𝔤 (dots denote images). The condition becomes ε̇·u'(σ)̇·α̇'·σ̇·τ̇ ∈ {1, τ̇}, equivalently ε̇·u'(σ)̇·α̇'·σ̇ ∈ {1, τ̇}.
- Case ε'_3 = 1, so α̇' = 1: the product lies in the + coset, which forces ε̇·u'(σ)̇·σ̇ = 1 (*).
- Case ε'_3 = −1, so α̇' = τ̇: moving τ̇ past σ̇ (using τσ = −στ) gives −ε̇·u'(σ)̇·σ̇ = 1 (**).
- Uniformly this reads u'(σ)̇ = (εε'_3)·σ̇^{-1} = (−εε'_3)·σ̇, using σ^{-1} = −σ; this is (9).
- Hypothesis (b) on u' gives u'(σ)̇ = ε'_2·σ̇. So it suffices to take ε = −ε'_2ε'_3.

Put τ' = τσ. Then α_0σ = ατσ = ατ' (implicitly τ² = 1), and στ = −τ'. This yields (10): α'' = ε'_2ε'_3·u'(ατ')·(α'τ'). The formula makes sense because ε_𝔖(ατ') = (−1)(−1) = 1, so ατ' ∈ 𝔖^+ and u'(ατ') is defined. Moreover α'' ∈ 𝔖^𝔤_τ and ε_𝔖(α'') = ε_𝔖(α)ε_𝔖(α') (11), so the sign ε_3 is multiplicative. Together with case (7) this finishes the proof that the composite u'u again satisfies (a), so the (a)(b)-automorphisms are closed under composition. The purpose is to define cleanly the group Z_{ρ,σ} ⊂ Aut(𝔖^+), which the next page identifies with 𝓜[0] (Teichmüller-tower / GT-type groups) in the universal cases.
errors: No substantive error. The sign bookkeeping checks out: (*) and (**) combine to u'(σ)̇ = εε'_3σ̇^{-1} = −εε'_3σ̇, which gives ε = −ε'_2ε'_3, and (10) follows from α'' = −ε'_2ε'_3·u'(ατ')·α'·(−τ').

Implicit assumptions not stated on the page: τ² = 1, or at least τ̇² = 1 mod 𝔖^𝔤, which is needed for {1,τ̇}τ̇^{-1} = {1,τ̇} and α_0 = ατ. Also, the factors u'(α_0) and u'(σ) are merged into u'(α_0σ) using that u' is a homomorphism on 𝔖^+, although u'(α_0) alone need not be defined if α_0 ∉ 𝔖^+. The previous page asserts α_0 ∈ 𝔖^𝔤 ⊂ 𝔖^+, so this is fine.
The verification that condition (b) is preserved under composition is not on this page; presumably it is done elsewhere or is regarded as immediate.

ideas.what: Closure under composition of the set of automorphisms of a profinite SL2-type group that send ρ to a conjugate of ρ^{±1} (twisted by τ) and σ to ±σ modulo a normal subgroup. The sign ε_3 behaves as a multiplicative character, and the central sign ε is adjusted to stay in 𝔖^𝔤_τ.
ideas.modern_name: Stabilizer-type subgroup of Aut(SL2(Z)^)/braid-type automorphism groups (Grothendieck–Teichmüller-style normalization conditions on generators of orders 4 and 6)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld, Ihara (GT and its variants); Lochak–Schneps for genus-one / SL2 aspects
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts; the Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the Teichmüller tower and GT-type ideas in general terms

ideas.what: Character ε_𝔖 (determinant sign) and the reflection τ' = τσ used to handle orientation-reversing conjugators.
ideas.modern_name: Extended (GL2 / mapping class with reflections) Teichmüller group, 'complex conjugation' component

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine sign-and-coset verification that a set of automorphisms forms a group. It is internal bookkeeping for the definition of Z_{ρ,σ}, whose identification with 𝓜[0] is on the next page, and contains no new idea on its own.
transcription_corrections: '𝔖^{∨G}' is better read as 𝔖^𝔤 (same symbol as on the previous page); likewise 𝔖^𝔤_τ.
Under the brace: 'ατσ = ατ''; τ' denotes τσ, and στ is marked as −τ'.
Penultimate line: 'on distingue les cas (*) et (**) de (9)', not 'u^{-1}(* a) de (7)'.
Last line: probably 'En combinaison avec le cas premier où ε_𝔖(α) = 1 (7), cela achève la démonstration' rather than 'M̄ combinaison'.
The crossed line before 'Or' reads roughly 'supposons maintenant qu'on a b) pour u'' / 'utilisant l'hyp. b) sur u''; the hypothesis is b), not 𝔖).
'u'(σ)̇ = ε'_2 σ̇' is preceded by a crossed-out attempt; the label is ε'_2.
